A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DKN/Neurological Topology Clustering study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-D support comparison despite retitling, redrawing and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on DKN acquisition, query perturbation, fact-checking and knowledge updating using GPT-2 and LLaMA2, with additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports additional neuron-control comparisons in the query-perturbation experiments.

M1.justification: AMIG localization, neuron-distance construction, persistent-homology clustering and filtering, and the suppression, enhancement and selective fine-tuning procedures are retained. Algorithm 1 is reformatted and explained more fully without an established procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same TempLAMA-derived factual queries, input perturbations, relation/golden fact-checking, new/old/rephrased knowledge and complex-text fact-checking. V2's revised dataset count does not correspond to identifiable new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 adds knowledge-neuron and random-neuron interventions as comparators for both suppression and enhancement, plus an explicit no-suppression comparison. Comparator membership in DKN acquisition, fact-checking and fine-tuning remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds a neuron-count-matched random control to the suppression evaluation. It also reverses the stated perturbation-change formula from the signed expression in v1 Figure 6 to a positive-decrease convention in Section 4.1. Models, perturbation operations and Appendix A thresholds are retained.

E4.justification: The existing query-perturbation ablations gain control evidence testing whether suppression and enhancement effects are specific to DKNs. The parameter-overlap, knowledge-retention and rephrasing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2's redrawn line plots in Figure 4 and Appendix D introduce translucent bands around curves. Neither captions nor text explain whether these represent uncertainty or graphical styling, and neither version specifies repeated runs or seeds. A statistical-reporting change cannot be reliably established.

E6.justification: V2 adds robustness-control results and revises perturbation-specific enhancement scores and averages. Several Table 1 entries are reconciled with v1's appendix: GPT-2/DBSCAN at two BDCs changes from 18 -> 39 to 12 -> 26. Appendix results also change, including LLaMA2/K-Means at 13 BDCs from 9.7 -> 9.1 to 19.7 -> 19.2. These materially revise multiple result sets, while fact-checking and fine-tuning outcomes are retained.

T1.justification: The DKN definitions, distance construction, complexity hypotheses, integrated-gradient equations and persistent-homology mathematics in Appendices B-C are retained. Equation 7 expands the existing occurrence-count notation without establishing a different intended definition or new theoretical result.

C1.justification: V2 withdraws the separately named Neuro-Degeneracy Analytic Framework contribution and its claim of a uniquely integrated holistic evaluation. It instead presents an investigation of relationships among degeneracy, robustness, evolvability and complexity, retaining the DKN-definition, NTC and principal empirical claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly attributes relation-based fact-checking imprecision to mismatches introduced by aggregation and filtering in Table 2's caption. Figure 9 also states that practical fine-tuning requires high, balanced accuracy across the evaluated datasets. The principal interpretations and model, knowledge-type and language limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the hardware, software versions, thresholds, filtering rules and complex-text prompt. The localization details are also retained, and both abstracts continue to promise code availability without providing a release.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds research on skill and language-specific neurons and critiques of knowledge-neuron interpretations, citing Wang et al. (2022), Tang et al. (2024), Niu et al. (2024), Bricken et al. (2023) and Chen et al. (2024b). This modestly broadens the positioning while retaining the existing research lineage.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, experimental explanations and findings. It removes the named-framework narrative, expands explanations of definitions and comparisons, and systematically replaces attenuation terminology with suppression.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the conceptual diagrams, replaces the unified methodology overview with separate workflow illustrations, expands the robustness displays and converts the enhancement and fine-tuning tables into bar charts. Acquisition curves are redisplayed across more main-text panels, and Appendix D plots are restyled and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the robustness evidence with neuron controls, resolves several main-table/appendix inconsistencies and improves explanatory clarity. These gains are limited by remaining numerical inconsistencies, undefined plot bands and reduced access to exact fine-tuning scores after their conversion to bar charts. The evidence supports a modest net improvement.
